chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Ali ibn Aban, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who performs the ritual bath (ghusl) in Medina for his Ihram; does that suffice for him in place of the Ghusl of Dhi al-Hulayfah? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ihram, the state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.غُسْلِ ذِي الْحُلَيْفَةِ: The ritual bath of Dhi al-Hulayfah, a specific Miqat near Medina

ai.seo_question: Does the ritual bath taken in Medina for Ihram replace the Ghusl of Dhi al-Hulayfah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that the ritual bath taken in Medina for Ihram suffices as the Ghusl of Dhi al-Hulayfah, illustrating the Shia principle that the Miqat is defined by the city's boundary rather than a specific physical spot. This ruling facilitates the pilgrim's journey by allowing the essential purification to be performed within the urban area before reaching the traditional boundary marker.
